thread:
Ava: heads up — saw ~20% p99 latency bump on int8-prod after merge 0a1b2c3. Appears correlated with KV cache eviction spikes. CI perf-alert flagged the canary.
Ravi: :eyes: linking perf dashboard and raw traces: https://ci.redwood/rt/perf/2165/artifacts — graphs show p99 jump around 10:12 UTC.
perf-bot: CI perf test (int8-latency) increased 18% vs baseline. Artifact: https://ci.redwood/short/2165.
Marta: anyone remember what landed in that merge? I saw "kselector-opt" and a refactor in kv prefetch.
Egor: yeah that was mine — combined kernel-selector heuristics + KV prefetch refactor. Passed unit tests and local perf runs.
Jon: quick ask — can we get a flame or top-down from a host that saw the spike? My first instinct: dequant memcpy overhead or packing changed.
Ava: attached a condensed flame snippet from host-17 around the regression window:
```
CPU: top down
42.1%  dequant_copy_and_pack
12.3%  kernel_selector::choose
8.6%   kv_cache::evict_if_needed
```
Ravi: also observed: batch=1 long-context traces show KV eviction/sec spiking from ~120 -> ~700 after that merge for the same workload.
perf-bot: Telemetry snapshot: host-17 evictions/sec 120 -> 705, avg cache occupancy down 60%. Telemetry commit tag: 0a1b2c3.
Marta: that fits — the prefetch refactor changed buffer layout and added an aggressive prefetch window that appears to alias with our KV backing store for small batches. Could increase memcpy churn.
Egor: I can open a revert PR quickly but want to confirm root cause first. Bisect might pinpoint the exact commit in the merge stack.
Jon: agree bisect. If it's the layout change in the packer, that's actionable. @Ravi can you run a bisect job on staging with the int8 latency harness? Keep the same seed/inputs as the canary.
Ravi: started bisect job 2165432130 — doing ~5k trace runs across commit slices, will post p99 deltas.
Ravi: bisect results: commit range points to 0d4f5a6 (quant pack layout change) as introducing the regression. The bundle that touched prefetch heuristics made it visible in production.
Ava: marking int8 canary rollout as HOLD in console and adding note: "hold - KV eviction regression after quant pack layout change". :no_entry:
Marta: quick mitigation: runtime flag to prefer legacy packer and disable aggressive prefetch for int8 canary. Something like:
```
quant.packer.mode = legacy
quant.prefetch.window = 0
```
Egor: pushed a patch to add the flags and a hotfix image to staging. After toggling legacy packer the p99 dropped back to baseline on the same traces.
Jon: good catch. We'll keep the canary held and ship the hotfix to prod if staging looks clean for 2 hours. Also add an explicit regression test measuring eviction rate across seqlen buckets.
perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-4821, linked artifacts and bisect output.
Marta: follow-ups: 1) revert or refactor packer layout to avoid aliasing with KV pages; 2) add automated eviction-rate regression test in CI; 3) add telemetry alert on sustained evictions/sec increase.
Egor: I'll prepare a cleaner refactor that preserves old layout or adds alignment padding. Will also add unit tests for pack/unpack.
Ava: thanks all. Keeping thread open until PR lands and canary unblocks.
Ravi: ack.
Jon: ack.
perf-bot: CI alert cleared on staging after hotfix applied.
